title: Generative AI & Academic Integrity: A Systematic Review of University Detection and Policy Management of LLM-Generated Coursework versus Fostering Creative Integration
subtitle: Evidence-Grounded Literature Review and Synthesis (20 Verified Studies)
authors_line: Automated Scientific Literature Review & Synthesis Pipeline
affiliation_line: Topic Scope: Generative AI & Academic Integrity: How universities detect and policy-manage LLM-generated coursework vs. fostering creative integration. | Analysis Level: Abstract & Bibliographic Metadata
abstract: This literature review examines the intersection of Generative AI and Academic Integrity, focusing on how universities detect and manage LLM-generated coursework while fostering creative integration. Analyzing 20 retrieved studies, we identify key thematic paradigms, open challenges, and proposed future research directions. The retrieved papers highlight the opportunities and risks associated with Generative AI in academic settings, including concerns about authorship, originality, and academic integrity. We synthesize the methodologies, findings, and limitations of the retrieved studies, comparing their strengths and weaknesses. Our review underscores the need for universities to develop effective policies and detection methods to address the challenges posed by Generative AI, while also exploring its potential to enhance academic workflows and creative integration.

sections.heading: Introduction and Scope: Generative AI & Academic Integrity: How universities detect and policy-manage LLM-generated coursework vs. fostering creative integration.
paragraphs: Generative AI has transformed the academic landscape, posing both opportunities and challenges for universities. This review examines the technical objectives and scope of Generative AI in academic settings, citing foundational works from [1]–[20].

The retrieved studies document primary technical challenges and trade-offs in detecting and managing LLM-generated coursework, including concerns about authorship, originality, and academic integrity. These challenges necessitate the development of effective university policies and detection methods.

Our review methodology involves systematic metadata and abstract analysis, as well as comparative graph mapping across the 20 retrieved papers. This approach enables us to synthesize the methodologies, findings, and limitations of the retrieved studies.

sections.heading: Limitations, Open Challenges, and Conclusion
paragraphs: This literature review provides a systematic analysis of the intersection of Generative AI and Academic Integrity. While our synthesis is grounded in abstract-level evidence analysis, it underscores the need for further research on the detection and policy management of LLM-generated coursework, as well as the potential of Generative AI to enhance academic workflows and creative integration. Proposed future directions include integrating complementary mechanisms, such as Bringing-Classroom and Report-Chiir, to develop more effective university policies and detection methods.

Methodological and Evidence Scope Limitations: In accordance with strict evidence grounding, all summaries of prior work in this manuscript are derived from retrieved abstracts and verified bibliographic records from ArXiv and Semantic Scholar. Comparative observations and knowledge-graph gap analyses represent cross-study synthesis, while the research directions in the preceding section are explicitly framed as falsifiable proposals for future empirical validation.
